peers.name: Manoj Vaibhav Gems N Jewellers Limited

bull_bear.body:
- The capacity expansion was funded internally - "Approx. =15 crore invested via internal accruals" - while the equity listing is presented as the growth-funding event: "Listing of the company enabled growth funds" and "Listed on both NSE and BSE".
- Business is explicitly working-capital intensive: "Our operations are working capital intensive, requiring adequate liquidity and funds to support business expansion and diversification across multiple locations", with a strategy to "Augment fund based capacities in order to scale up business operations".
- The historical balance sheet shows FY26 equity share capital of INR 96.4 Cr and other equity of INR 581.4 Cr (versus 72.1 and 128.7 in FY25), FY26 current borrowings of INR 179.3 Cr and no non-current borrowings, alongside inventories of INR 439.4 Cr and trade receivables of INR 235.7 Cr.
- FY26 cash flow shows Changes in Working Capital of -408.0 and Net Cash from Operating Activities of -281.7, against Cash Flow from Financing Activities of 410.3 - i.e. growth was funded by financing inflows, not operations.
- The deck makes no mention of any dividend or buyback policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Headline claim is "Largest B2B Manufacturer of Mangalsutras in India", with "15+ Years of Heritage & Craftsmanship" and "Pan-India Presence in 24 states and 4UTs".
- Client franchise is institutional: "Marquee Institutional Clientele such as Titan and Malabar Gold", with the deck listing relationship tenures - Waman Hari Pethe Jewellers (15 years), Kudbe Jewellers (15 years), Joyalukkas India (14 years), Arundhati Jewellers (14 years), Titan Company (13 years) and Reliance Retail (13 years).
- Overseas and emerging partnerships named include Goldbox Enterprises (UK) (7 years), Sona Sansaar (New Zealand) (11 years), Damas Jewellery LLC (UAE) (3 years) and Novel Jewels Limited (Aditya Birla Group) (2.5 years).
- Competitive edge framed on three legs: "Distinctive Designs Backed by Product Depth", "Integrated Manufacturing Capabilities" and "Experienced Leadership that Powers Growth"; milestones cited include being "the first in India to manufacture and launch a 24K gold mangalsutra" and being "Honoured with Excellence in Self-Certification Level-1 by Titan Company Limited".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Formalisation] Industry shift is a stated tailwind: "Formalisation, driven by factors such as compulsory hallmarking, GST compliance, and consumer demand for transparency has led to market consolidation towards organised retail", with organised manufacturers at "a share of 10.9% in the wholesale gold jewellery market, in India" in CY23.
- [Market size] Segment "expected to reach a value of 489 billion by CY29, representing a CAGR of 9.0% from CY24 to CY29" (source cited as CareEdge Report).
- [Category structure] "Traditional designs dominate the category with 62.3% share"; "South India leads regional demand with 39.7% market share, followed by West & Central at 26.9%".
- [Bridal opportunity] Per the Redseer Industry Report cited, "bridal jewellery accounting for the highest share at 23-25% of total wedding costs" and "An average of 30 to 250 grams of gold is consumed in marriages across India", costing between INR 0.15 million and INR 1.3 million.
- [Promoter-led board] Chairman & MD Chetan N Thadeshwar has "over forty (40) years of experience in the jewellery industry"; CEO Viraj C Thadeshwar and COO Balraj C Thadeshwar are executive directors, with Mamta C Thadeshwar as a non-executive director.

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Shringar House of Mangalsutra as India's largest B2B manufacturer of mangalsutras - "THE GOLD STANDARD IN MANGALSUTRA" - supplying marquee institutional jewellery chains from an integrated 4,000 kg p.a. facility, and now extending from its core mangalsutra category into bridal jewellery.
